info.title: StampMitra Developer API
info.summary: Indian identity verification and e-Stamp Paper APIs for the StampMitra developer portal.
info.description:
The API-key Developer Suite: verification (PAN, GSTIN, vehicle RC, Voter ID, Driving Licence, Passport, CIN, Udyam, bank account), e-Stamp Paper (catalogue, duty, typed orders, stamps, PAN card, certificates), the Service wallet (one balance for verification calls and e-Stamp service charges) and the Stamp Duty wallet, usage and request logs, and webhook events. Generated from the same data as the docs at https://developer.stampmitra.in.

Authentication: send your API key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `x-api-key: <key>`. Sandbox keys (sk_test_) and production keys (sk_live_) use the same host; the key prefix selects the environment. Sandbox keys are free and get 20% of each endpoint's production rate limit (minimum 1 request per window); production calls are metered per successful call. Every API also has a daily limit per organisation and environment (calls per API per day, reset at 00:00 IST): 100 on Sandbox, 100 on pay-as-you-go, 500 on Business, agreed per deal on a commercial plan. Over it the call gets 429 `DAILY_API_LIMIT_REACHED` and is not charged. Sandbox keys also keep two older limits next to it, both reset at 00:00 IST: 200 calls a day across all APIs for the organisation (`SANDBOX_DAILY_LIMIT`) and 50 sandbox calls a day from one IP address (`SANDBOX_IP_LIMIT`).

Errors: every error is `{ error: { code, message, requestId } }` (plus `field` where an input is at fault, and `details` on some errors: `details.errors[]` lists every finding of a rejected e-Stamp order body as `{ field, code, message, index }`, `details.wallet` names the wallet that is short on a 402). Send an `X-Request-Id` header and it is echoed back as `requestId`. See `x-error-codes`, which lists both the envelope codes and the per-field codes.

Idempotency: send an `Idempotency-Key` header on operations that accept it (metered verification and duty/parties calls, order creation, payment intents) to make retries safe. The same key and request replays the stored response; the same key with a different request is 422 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`; the same key while the first request is still running is 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS` with `Retry-After`. Keys are scoped to your organization, the route and the environment and are kept for 24 hours. `x-idempotent` and `x-retry-safe` mark each operation.

Response headers on authenticated calls (additive, safe to ignore): `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset` (seconds) on rate-limited routes, `X-RateLimit-Daily-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Daily-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Daily-Reset` (an ISO 8601 timestamp with +05:30) for the API called on metered verification routes, `Retry-After` on every 429 and 503, and for live keys `X-Wallet-State` (OK, LOW_BALANCE, FINISHED) and `X-Wallet-Balance-Low: true`. Read the exact balance with GET /v1/account/balance; guide: https://developer.stampmitra.in/docs/balance-usage-and-rate-limits.

Webhooks: outbound order events are signed. `x-webhook-signature` and the top-level `webhooks` section describe the headers and the HMAC-SHA256 construction.

Versioning: Contract version (info.version) follows semantic versioning, independent of the URL version (x-api-version: v1; every path is under /v1). MAJOR: any breaking change to the published contract (removed or renamed operationId, path, field or enum value; changed status code, error shape or required-ness; a /v2 prefix). Generated SDKs bump their major version too. MINOR: backwards-compatible additions (new endpoint, new optional request field, new response field, new error code or webhook event). Clients must ignore unknown response fields and treat unknown enum values as unknown-safe. PATCH: documentation, description and example corrections that do not change behaviour.

x-error-codes.description: Validation failed or the request was rejected, or error.code IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED: the route requires an Idempotency-Key header (e-Stamp order creation, batches). On the e-Stamp order routes the message starts with VALIDATION_FAILED and error.details.errors[] lists each finding.
Missing or invalid API key, or missing required scope.

Insufficient fulfilment wallet balance. On e-Stamp order creation the message names the wallet that is short and error.details.wallet is STAMP_DUTY or SERVICE_FEE; nothing was created or charged. Top up that wallet and retry with the same Idempotency-Key.

IP not allowed, plan entitlement not enabled, or limit reached. On the wallet routes a key without the wallet scope is refused (401 or 403): access depends on the key, ask support to enable the wallet scopes.
Resource not found.

State conflict (for example cancelling an order or stamp that is no longer in a cancellable state; the message says which state), or error.code IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS: a request with this Idempotency-Key is still being processed (retry the identical request after Retry-After).
Request understood but cannot be processed, or error.code IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED: the Idempotency-Key was already used with a different request.
Rate limit exceeded.
Unexpected error, and upstream failures (502, 503). The status distinguishes them.
Fallback for any other 4xx status.
POST /v1/estamp/orders was sent without an Idempotency-Key header. Nothing was created. Send a key and resend.
The Idempotency-Key is not 1 to 255 printable characters.
The Idempotency-Key was already used with a different request. Nothing was created or charged. Use a new key for a different request.
A request with this Idempotency-Key is still being processed. Resend the identical request after the Retry-After delay.
e-Stamp ordering is temporarily paused (validate and create). The message is customer-facing. Retry later with backoff.
The uploaded file is larger than 10 MB (POST /v1/estamp/orders/{orderId}/documents).
Only PDF, JPEG and PNG files are accepted: the declared type is something else, or the file has no recognised signature.
The file's first bytes do not match its declared content type, for example a PNG sent as application/pdf.
A wallet top-up amount is below the minimum. The message states the limit.
A wallet top-up amount is above the maximum. The message states the limit.
Sandbox keys only: the organization already has the maximum number of open or stored sandbox e-Stamp orders. Nothing was created. Open sandbox orders finish by themselves, or cancel them.
A required field is missing or empty, for example stamps[0].firstParty.name.
The wrong JSON type for the field.
A value outside the allowed list, for example a category that is not e_stamp or traditional_stamp.
A number that is zero or negative, or outside its minimum or maximum (for example quantity above 1000).
A text longer than its limit, for example a party name over 150 characters.
More than 5000 stamp lines in one order.
A field the API does not recognise. Unknown fields are rejected, not ignored.
firstParty, secondParty or propertyArea is an array or another shape. Send one object (a party may also be a name string).
propertyArea.unit is not exactly one of Square Feet, Square Yard, Square Meters, Not Applicable.
panCardImage is not an https link on the default port without credentials.
Stamp lines for more than one state in one order. Create one order per state.
The state is not accepting orders right now. Check GET /v1/estamp/states/availability and retry later.
The state sells stamps only in whole multiples of a fixed step. See denomination.multipleOf in GET /v1/estamp/states/{stateCode}/requirements.
The panCardImage link was refused: it must be an https link (default port, no login) to the payer's PAN card.
stampDutyPayer is not the first or second party's name, FIRST_PARTY or SECOND_PARTY (SECOND_PARTY needs a second party).

get.description: Machine-readable field requirements for a state and, optionally, an article, a denomination and a category. post.description: LEGACY generic order endpoint, kept for existing integrations. To order e-Stamps use `POST /v1/estamp/orders` (and `POST /v1/estamp/orders/validate` first): it takes typed `stamps[]` lines with `state`, `articleCode`, `denomination`, `firstParty`, `secondParty`, `propertyArea` and the payer's `panCardImage`, and is checked field by field. post.summary: Validate an e-Stamp order before creating it
post.description: Runs the same validation StampMitra applies at order-creation time WITHOUT saving anything and without charging. Use it to surface field-level problems and pricing warnings to your own users before calling POST /v1/estamp/orders. HTTP success whether the result is READY_TO_PLACE, WARNINGS or NEEDS_INFORMATION (today 201, the default for a POST here, not 200: treat any 2xx as success); a 400 is returned only for a body that cannot be accepted, and then `error.details.errors[]` lists each finding as { field, code, message, index }. `documentsRequired` says whether a PAN card is advisable for the state; it is never blocking. Requires the `estamp.orders.validate` scope. Rate limit: 30 requests per 60 seconds.

201.description: Success, same body as 200. The backend documents 200 but NestJS defaults POST handlers to 201, so clients must accept any 2xx.

400.description: VALIDATION_FAILED: the body is malformed or a stamp line cannot be accepted. error.details.errors[] lists each finding as { field, code, message, index }; see x-error-codes for the codes.

error.message: VALIDATION_FAILED: stamps[0].firstParty.name: name is required

409.description: SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE: e-Stamp ordering is temporarily paused. The message is customer-facing. Retry later with backoff.

error.message: E-Stamp ordering is temporarily paused. Please try again shortly.

post.summary: Create an e-Stamp order (pending internal review)
post.description: Creates an e-Stamp order. This reaches StampMitra's validation stage and debits the duty from your Stamp Duty Wallet and the service charges (99 procurement + 5 API charge per paper, plus 18% GST collected at top-up) from your Service wallet, the same balance that pays for verification calls; it does NOT place the order with the issuing vendor, because a person confirms placement separately. The returned `status` is therefore a pre-placement status (PENDING_REVIEW on a live key), never a completed order. Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header: the same key and the same body replays the original response, with no second order and no second debit. A short wallet is a 402 PAYMENT_REQUIRED naming the wallet (`error.details.wallet` is STAMP_DUTY or SERVICE_FEE), and nothing is created. Requires the `estamp.orders.create` scope. Rate limit: 30 requests per 60 seconds. Where the per-order API fee is enabled for your account, one charge applies per created order.

error.message: VALIDATION_FAILED: stamps[0].articleCode: articleCode is required

Nothing was created and nothing was charged. Top up that wallet and retry with the same Idempotency-Key.

error.message: The Stamp Duty Wallet balance is too low for this order. Top up the Stamp Duty Wallet and retry with the same Idempotency-Key. Nothing was created or charged.

error.message: A request with this Idempotency-Key is being processed; retry shortly with the same key

get.description: Your organization's own orders only, newest first. `items` and `nextCursor` are the contract: pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` to continue, and it is null on the last page. `data` repeats `items` and `pagination` carries page, limit and total for clients that read the earlier fields (total is exact on the last page and null while more pages follow; page numbers beyond 20 are refused, continue with the cursor). post.summary: Create a Razorpay order to top up the Stamp Duty Wallet
post.description: Returns the Razorpay order to complete in Checkout. The terms: a processing fee of 6% of `baseAmount` is added on top, plus 18% GST on that fee, and a GST tax invoice is issued for the fee (see the invoices routes; `topupId` is the invoice id). `baseAmount`, `gstAmount` and `totalCharged` are JSON numbers, every other amount is a string. The wallet is credited with `creditAmount`, which is `baseAmount` in full; the fee and the GST are not credited, and stamp duty itself carries no GST. The response shows the fee, the GST and the total to pay (`totalCharged`): show your payer those figures, not numbers you calculated, because the rate can change. The credit arrives automatically when the payment succeeds. A `baseAmount` outside the allowed range is a 400 AMOUNT_BELOW_MINIMUM or AMOUNT_ABOVE_MAXIMUM. Requires the `stamp-duty-wallet.topup` scope. Rate limit: 20 requests per 60 seconds. Access depends on the key: if you get 401 or 403, ask support to enable the wallet scopes. post.description: Attaches the stamp-duty payer's PAN card (PDF, JPEG or PNG, at most 10 MB) to an order as multipart/form-data: a `file` part and an optional `type` part (only `pan_card`). IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Optional client-generated key (1 to 255 printable characters) that makes a retried POST safe. A key is scoped to your organization, the route and the environment (a sandbox key never matches a live one) and is kept for 24 hours. Retrying with the same key and the same request replays the original response (same status and body) without repeating the work or billing again. The same key with a different request returns 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED. The same key while the first request is still being processed returns 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS with a Retry-After header. Routes that require the key (POST /v1/estamp/orders, POST /v1/batches) answer 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED without it.

IdempotencyKeyRequired.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKeyRequired.description: REQUIRED. A unique key (1 to 255 printable characters) per logical order-creation attempt: an order spends money, so it must never be retriable by accident. Derive it from something stable you own (an agreement id plus a version, for example lease-2026-0412-v1), persist it before you send, and change it when you change the body. A key is scoped to your organization, the route and the environment and is kept for 24 hours. A retried request with the same key and the same body replays the original response (same status and body) without creating a second order or debiting again; the same key with a different body is 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; the same key while the first request is still being processed is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS with a Retry-After header. A missing key is 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED and nothing is created.
